question: Gastric glands present in the wall of the stomach do NOT release:
solution:
The correct answer is __**saliva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The gastric glands in the stomach are responsible for secreting various substances that aid in digestion.
 
• These glands release pepsinogen, which is converted to pepsin in the presence of hydrochloric acid.
 
• Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is secreted by the parietal cells in the gastric glands and helps in maintaining an acidic environment.
 
• Mucus is also secreted by the gastric glands to protect the stomach lining from the corrosive effects of HCl and digestive enzymes.
 
• Saliva is not secreted by the gastric glands; it is produced by the salivary glands located in the mouth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pepsinogen**: An inactive enzyme precursor secreted by the chief cells in the stomach, which is activated to pepsin by the acidic environment.
 
• **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**: Produced by the parietal cells in the stomach, it creates an acidic environment, which is essential for the activation of pepsin and for killing pathogens.
 
• **Mucus**: Secreted by the mucous cells in the stomach lining, it forms a protective barrier to prevent the stomach lining from being digested by gastric juices.
 
• **Saliva**: A digestive fluid produced by the salivary glands in the mouth, containing enzymes like amylase that begin the process of digestion.
 
• **Gastric Glands**: Located in the lining of the stomach, these glands include mucous cells, parietal cells, and chief cells, each secreting different substances necessary for digestion.
